model_fitness.best_available_model: D2-mdx (DBA/2J-mdx) mouse, which unlike classic C57BL/10-mdx develops substantial endomysial fibrosis and fat replacement and measurable diaphragm/cardiac involvement; secondary model = primary human DMD fibro-adipogenic progenitor (FAP) / myotube co-culture for ligand-redundancy mapping.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: INFERENCE (supportive): the mechanism at stake is TGF-beta/CTGF/myostatin-driven fibro-adipogenic remodelling in dystrophin-null muscle, which a fibrotic dystrophic mouse reproduces in the correct extracellular compartment. EVIDENCE (contradictory, PMID 32522498; NCT04632940; NCT04371666): no model so far has predicted the human functional outcome for this mechanism - both ligand-blockade agents engaged target in humans and failed on function, so the models used previously were not predictive of function.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes for FAPs, macrophages, myofibers and cardiac fibroblasts - all extracellular-facing, which is exactly the compartment an IgG or Fc-fusion can reach. Human FAP culture captures the fibrogenic executor cell directly.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Primary: absolute and specific tetanic force of diaphragm strips and EDL ex vivo. Secondary: hydroxyproline content, Sirius-red fibrotic area, adipocyte fraction, and antibody concentration measured in diaphragm and myocardium homogenate (compartment exposure).
model_fitness.important_limitations: Mouse lifespan precludes the decade-scale remodelling that caps human benefit; murine IgG pharmacokinetics and muscle interstitial penetration differ from paediatric human dosing; and D2-mdx fibrosis is partly developmental rather than purely contraction-induced. Crucially, this model class has already failed to predict two human negatives, so a positive result here is weak evidence and only a negative result is strongly decision-making.

plan.critical_question: Is any single secreted ligand load-bearing in dystrophic fibro-fatty remodelling, or is the network redundant such that neutralising one node is absorbed? Equivalently: can combined multi-ligand blockade produce a contractile-force benefit that single-ligand blockade (already twice negative in humans) could not?
plan.proposed_experiment: Randomised, blinded, placebo-controlled study in D2-mdx mice (n=12-15/arm, both sexes, treatment from 4 weeks to 6 months to model early initiation). Five arms: (1) vehicle; (2) anti-CTGF/CCN2 surrogate mAb; (3) anti-myostatin/activin ligand trap (e.g. soluble ActRIIB-Fc or anti-myostatin mAb); (4) combined anti-CTGF + anti-myostatin/activin; (5) givinostat as the positive mechanistic comparator (the one agent in this pathway with a positive human functional trial, PMID 38508835). Primary endpoint is ex vivo specific tetanic force of the diaphragm. Mandatory embedded pharmacology: measure antibody concentration in diaphragm and left-ventricular homogenate versus plasma at steady state, because no DMD biologic programme has ever demonstrated exposure in the compartments that drive mortality. Pre-specify that histology alone does not count as success.
plan.model: D2-mdx mouse (fibrotic, fat-replacing dystrophic model with diaphragm and cardiac involvement), with a parallel human DMD FAP/myotube co-culture arm to map which ligands are required for collagen and adipocyte output when blocked singly versus in combination.
plan.primary_readout: Ex vivo specific force (N/cm2) of diaphragm strips, with EDL force and hydroxyproline/Sirius-red fibrotic fraction as key secondary readouts, plus measured diaphragm and myocardial antibody concentration as a go/no-go pharmacology gate.
plan.supportive_result: Combined multi-ligand blockade (arm 4) produces a significant increase in diaphragm specific force versus vehicle that exceeds either single-ligand arm and approaches the givinostat comparator, AND measured antibody concentration in diaphragm/myocardium is pharmacologically meaningful (detectable at or above the in vitro IC50 for ligand neutralisation). This would indicate the prior human failures reflected single-node redundancy rather than an intrinsically unproductive axis, and would justify designing a combination biologic programme.
plan.negative_result: Combination blockade produces no significant diaphragm force benefit over vehicle despite confirmed ligand suppression (reduced free CTGF/myostatin in plasma and muscle), and/or antibody concentration in diaphragm and myocardium is negligible. Either outcome reproduces the pamrevlumab/domagrozumab pattern of target engagement without function (PMID 32522498; NCT04632940; NCT04371666) and extends it to the combination case.
plan.decision_enabled: Negative result: stop the protein arm for this patient and this hypothesis - deprioritise all secreted-ligand neutralisation as a degeneration brake and concentrate downstream-brake resources on the approved small-molecule arm (givinostat) plus the dystrophin-restoration gating assays. This is the invalidating experiment the arm needs and it should be run before any further biologic investment. Supportive result: a combination biologic is worth a formal preclinical package, but note the bar is high given two Phase 3 and one Phase 2 human failures, and sponsorship would realistically require a partner rather than a foundation-scale effort. A pure exposure failure (no antibody in diaphragm/heart) converts the conclusion to NO PLAUSIBLE DELIVERY PATH for the compartments that determine survival.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Two complementary models, because two distinct decisions are at stake. (A) Patient-derived exon-55-nonsense myogenic cells - urine-derived or fibroblast-derived MyoD-transdifferentiated myotubes from this specific patient - for the drug-interaction/NMD question. (B) D2-mdx mouse with longitudinal diaphragm and cardiac endpoints for the mortality-compartment question.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Model A: EVIDENCE-adjacent and directly on point - it contains the actual exon 55 PTC and therefore reports faithfully on whether HDAC inhibition changes mutant DMD transcript abundance, NMD efficiency, or readthrough yield (the stated unstudied combination risk, HYPOTHESIS, not_studied). Model B: INFERENCE (supportive) - captures fibro-adipogenic remodelling, necrosis and regeneration, the processes givinostat is known to modify in human muscle (EVIDENCE, PMID 27566866), in the diaphragm and heart where human data are absent (INFERENCE, not_studied, PMID 38508835).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Model A captures the myofiber lineage carrying the patient's own allele, which is the only cell type in which the transcript-level interaction question is meaningful; it does NOT contain FAPs or macrophages, so it cannot address fibrosis. Model B captures FAPs, macrophages, satellite cells, myofibers and cardiomyocytes together.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Model A: DMD mRNA abundance by allele-aware RT-qPCR/ddPCR with and without a translation-inhibitor NMD block, plus full-length dystrophin protein by capillary western - all +/- givinostat and +/- a readthrough agent. Model B: diaphragm ex vivo specific force, respiratory function (whole-body plethysmography), echocardiographic fractional shortening/ejection fraction, and cardiac/diaphragm fibrosis by hydroxyproline.
model_fitness.important_limitations: Transdifferentiated myotubes are immature, lack mechanical loading, and have non-physiological NMD and HDAC-target stoichiometry, so an absence of interaction in vitro does not fully exclude one in vivo. D2-mdx cardiac disease is milder and far faster than the human decades-long cardiomyopathy, so it can detect a direction of effect but cannot quantify human cardiac benefit. Neither model can answer whether slowing ambulatory decline translates to human survival - only long-term cardiorespiratory follow-up of treated patients can.

plan.critical_question: Two gating questions, both cheap. (1) Does HDAC inhibition interfere with, or usefully potentiate, a future dystrophin-restoring readthrough arm by changing mutant DMD transcript level, NMD efficiency or readthrough yield in this patient's own cells? (2) Does HDAC inhibition improve diaphragm and cardiac function - the compartments that cause death - or only the ambulatory skeletal-muscle compartment in which it was validated?
plan.proposed_experiment: Experiment 1 (primary, run first; weeks not months). Derive myogenic cells from this patient (urine-derived cells or dermal fibroblasts, MyoD-transdifferentiated) plus a non-DMD control and, if obtainable, a second DMD nonsense line. Treat with givinostat at clinically achievable concentrations, a readthrough agent, both, and vehicle, each +/- an NMD inhibitor to quantify allele decay. Read out DMD mRNA by ddPCR and full-length dystrophin by capillary western. This single experiment simultaneously serves as the NMD/readthrough-amenability gating assay flagged as the top unknown for this allele, so it is doubly cost-efficient. Experiment 2 (confirmatory, parallel if resources allow). D2-mdx mice, givinostat versus vehicle on background corticosteroid, dosed from 4 weeks to 9-12 months, with pre-specified primary endpoint of diaphragm ex vivo specific force and co-primary echocardiographic fractional shortening - i.e. deliberately NOT a limb timed-function surrogate.
plan.model: Patient-derived exon-55-nonsense myotubes (Experiment 1); D2-mdx mouse with diaphragm and cardiac endpoints (Experiment 2).
plan.primary_readout: Experiment 1: fold-change in DMD transcript abundance and in full-length dystrophin protein under givinostat alone and in combination with readthrough, relative to vehicle. Experiment 2: diaphragm specific force and left-ventricular fractional shortening versus vehicle.
plan.supportive_result: Experiment 1: givinostat is neutral or increases mutant DMD transcript abundance and does not reduce readthrough-generated dystrophin - meaning the two arms are combinable, and the patient can stay on the approved brake while readthrough is pursued. Experiment 2: significant preservation of diaphragm force and/or fractional shortening, which would be the first mechanistic support that this arm touches the causes of death rather than only an ambulatory surrogate.
plan.negative_result: Experiment 1: givinostat measurably reduces mutant DMD transcript or suppresses readthrough-generated dystrophin - a real, specific combination antagonism that would force sequencing rather than co-administration of the two arms. Experiment 2: no diaphragm or cardiac benefit despite the expected reduction in limb-muscle fibrosis - which would confirm the arm's biggest failure mode (benefit confined to the compartment that does not cause death) and would reset family expectations about what the approved drug can and cannot buy.
plan.decision_enabled: Experiment 1 is the highest-value next action for this patient overall, because it is simultaneously the readthrough gating assay and the combination-safety assay; its result determines whether the downstream brake and a dystrophin-restoring arm are run together or in sequence, and whether readthrough has any substrate at all. Experiment 2 does not change whether to use the approved drug now - the controlled human functional evidence (PMID 38508835) and approval (PMID 38967716) already justify genotype-agnostic use today, and INFERENCE strongly favours early initiation before fibro-fatty replacement caps benefit - but it determines how the benefit should be described to the family and whether cardiorespiratory monitoring should be intensified or additional cardioprotective therapy sought independently. Neither experiment should delay starting the approved agent.
